title: Block Followers to Cut Off a User
statement:
A social network has `n` members, each with a distinct integer member id. There are `e` directed follow links. The link `p q` means member `p` follows member `q`, and a message can be sent from `p` to `q` along it. A message only travels from a follower to the member being followed, and a member can forward any message they receive.

React expert `A` is constantly troubled by React newbie `B`, who keeps sending messages that get forwarded along links until they reach `A`. `A` can stop this by removing some of the members who **directly follow `A`** (the members `p` with a link `p A`), which deletes their links into `A`. No other link can be removed.

Find the **minimum** set of direct followers of `A` that must be removed so that `B` can no longer reach `A` by any chain of links. (This minimum set is unique.) If `B` already cannot reach `A`, the set is empty.

A and B are different members. Links may repeat, and a member may follow themselves; neither affects the answer.
inputFormat: The first line contains `n`. The second line contains the `n` distinct member ids. The next line contains `e`, followed by `e` lines, each with two integers `p q`. The last two lines contain `A` and `B`.
outputFormat: Print one line: the size `k` of the set, followed by the `k` member ids in increasing order, all separated by single spaces. If the set is empty, print `0`.

examples.explanation: Member 6 sends to 3 (6 -> 3) and to 5 (6 -> 5). Member 5 reaches 2, and 3 follows 1 directly. The direct followers of 1 are 2, 3 and 4. Members 2 and 3 are reachable from 6, but 4 is not, so removing 2 and 3 is necessary and enough.
The only chain is 40 -> 30 -> 20 -> 10. A = 10 has a single direct follower, 20, and removing it cuts the chain.
Member 3 has no outgoing link, so it cannot reach 1 even though 1 has a follower.

hints: Every path from `B` to `A` ends with a link `p A` for some direct follower `p`. Which of those followers is it necessary to remove?
A direct follower `p` must be removed exactly when `B` can reach `p` (possibly `p = B` itself) without first passing through `A`. Removing any other follower never helps.
Run one BFS or iterative DFS from `B` that never enters `A`, then output the direct followers of `A` that were visited, sorted.
